About this model

A right-foot educational proxy, not medically accurate geometry. The big toe is medial; the fibula and fifth toe are lateral. This model includes 26 main foot bones, two hallux sesamoids, and the distal tibia and fibula (their malleoli are separate selectable components).

Detailed geometry and ligaments

Original sculpted bone surfaces show a talar body and neck, a shaped heel with sustentaculum and lateral tubercle, a navicular tuberosity, wedge-shaped cuneiforms, a cuboid plantar groove, and contoured long bones. These are illustrative landmarks, not segmented scans or validated joint surfaces.

18 selectable gold ligament bands include lateral, deltoid, syndesmosis, subtalar, and plantar connections. Five longitudinal bundles distinguish each band from the round tendons. End footprints follow their assigned bones; deformation, width, and positions are approximations. Deep bands may require reduced bone opacity. No tissue tension or collision-free ligament wrapping is calculated.

Anatomy reference: lateral ankle ligaments and deltoid overview. Geometry is original; no external anatomy meshes were added.

What is represented

Named bones, broad relative arrangement, the nine requested tendon groups, principal attachments, anterior versus retromalleolar routes, and four-way branching for the long toe flexors and extensors.

What is approximate

All shapes, dimensions, joint surfaces, tendon thicknesses and attachment coordinates are hand-authored. Tibialis posterior secondary insertions, toe extensor expansions, retinacula, sheaths, cartilage, muscles and individual variation are omitted.

Flexion rotates the talus and descendants around a transverse ankle pivot. Tilt uses an oblique hindfoot axis (80%) and an additional midfoot pivot (20%). This fixed split is illustrative, not a validated joint model. Toe joints are held neutral. The leg stays fixed.

Tendons follow bone-bound routing points and approximate surface-clearance envelopes. They can slide or change apparent length; contact, wrapping and tissue deformation are not biomechanically validated. Small intersections may remain near attachments or between tendons.

Assets and sources

No external anatomy meshes are used. The supplied procedural anatomy is original. BodyParts3D downloads and its current CC BY 4.0 license were checked on 13 September 2026. Its whole-body meshes require extraction, alignment and rigging before use here. Older releases and third-party mirrors may have different licenses.

Anatomical reference: Lhoste-Trouilloud, The tibialis posterior tendon (2012). Rendering: Three.js, MIT license.

iPhone & offline use

Open the HTTPS site in Safari, then use Share → Add to Home Screen. Essential app files are cached after a successful load where service workers are supported. Private hosting may still require an online sign-in. See the included README for local setup and independent HTTPS hosting.

Checking offline support…

Real iPhone/iPad Safari testing has not been performed. Home Screen installation, offline launches, multitouch, and WebGL recovery need real-device verification.
